text:
Both teams arrive on the back of a loss two days ago. Calgary dropped a 5-2 game at Colorado but is 3-2-0 in its last five, and it's missing Connor Zary and Samuel Honzek. San Jose was routed 5-1 by Ottawa at home, is 2-3-0 in its last five, and is without Alexander Wennberg and Igor Chernyshov, both on injured reserve. Ty Dellandrea has taken Wennberg's spot beside Marchment and Toffoli, and Collin Graf has stepped into Chernyshov's.

Neither side wins the chance battle at five on five: CGY has 47% of the expected goals (the quality of shots taken and allowed), SJS 44%. Calgary's record flatters no one, but our numbers say it's better than it looks, with a -16 goal difference against -7.0 expected, partly because of its goaltending. That's the matchup to watch. Projected starter Dustin Wolf is at -8.2 goals saved above expected this season, while projected Sharks starter Yaroslav Askarov is at +7.7 and has been strong over his last five starts. Calgary also takes 4.4 penalties a game, and San Jose's power play creates more (0.65 expected goals a game) than its penalty kill prevents.

Macklin Celebrini, the 2024 first overall pick, leads our probabilities at 43% to score and 82% for a point. For Calgary, Morgan Frost is one point from 200 career points. Our under-the-radar picks are Mikael Backlund (49% for a point) and Ryan Strome (18% to score), because San Jose gives up the most expected goals per 60 of any team.
